source: Invest Like the Best — Why the markets are pricing AI wrong: July 2026 AI/semis selloff, private inference cloud, old-GPU repricing, ~$700B Blackwell/Rubin credit gap
summary: Hyperscaler operating cash flows are already accelerating and consensus is modeling them to monetize Blackwell/Rubin at Ampere-era rates — a ~$700B underestimate
summary_extended: Baker argues that consensus analysts are making a critical error by modeling hyperscaler monetization of Blackwell and Rubin GPU generations at Ampere-era rates — two full GPU generations behind current pricing — leading to a ~$700B underestimate of hyperscaler operating cash flow. He supports this with concrete data: Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon operating cash flows accelerated from 28% to 32% growth this quarter, and when adjusted for one-time items like EU fines, the acceleration is even sharper at 28% to 35%. If hyperscalers monetize Blackwell and Rubin even at a discount to current market rates (rather than Ampere rates), aggregate hyperscale operating cash flow would be closer to $2T versus the consensus estimate of $1.3–1.4T. This $700B gap effectively removes the credit risk narrative — the bear case that hyperscalers cannot fund AI capex without dangerous levels of external borrowing — making that concern largely moot. The investment implication is that the hyperscalers themselves (MSFT, META, AMZN, GOOGL) are materially undervalued relative to their true cash generation capacity, and the AI infrastructure selloff of mid-2026 is mispriced.
